scope: re-evaluate the 'patch the dedrun reliableCommands' idea against what we already proved

key_realization.fact_we_already_had: the 2697 dedrun's own gamestate IS accepted by the 1649370 client - earlier sessions reached client phase 8 with the dedrun, which only happens after the client consumes the gamestate
key_realization.consequence: the gamestate format produced by the dedrun is compatible with our client; our replay failed because we lack the send context, not because the content is wrong

what_the_dedrun_has_that_we_lack: the exact challenge value at encode time
a non-empty lastClientCommandString that produces the observed key shift
a reliableSequence that frames the command as 'unacked' so it is retransmitted
its own SV_WriteReliableCommand wrapper (opcode + sequence + text)

why_replay_kept_failing.we_provided: raw body bytes and a constant key
why_replay_kept_failing.the_client_expected: a properly framed reliable command inside a netchan message, with a key derived from the server's live fields
why_replay_kept_failing.mismatch: even a byte-perfect body is rejected when the outer framing does not match what the client's parser expects

plan_2_refined.idea: do not replace the dedrun; use it as a framing engine by editing the command text it is about to retransmit
how: read client_t.reliableSequence and reliableAcknowledge (ack is 0, so commands 1..sequence are all pending)
read reliableCommands[1].command to see what the dedrun's first gamestate command text actually looks like
if it is the gamestate text, we can substitute our own text in place and let the dedrun's encoder frame and cipher it
plan_2_refined.value: this isolates 'content' from 'framing' definitively: if a substituted command is accepted, framing was never the problem; if it is rejected, the content is

next: start one dedrun session and dump reliableCommands[1..8] text
compare that text with the 1168-byte body we recovered from the wire
if the wire body is simply that text ciphered, we can reconstruct framing exactly
